offered.descriptor: Clean and modern museum-model look: crisp flat surfaces, sharp precise wells and slots, thin even lips, everything reading as machined and orderly with tidy uniform grooves and neatly filed notches; a quiet, engineered, almost architectural feel.

Weathered stone-canal heritage look: softly worn edges, gently rounded stone tiles that feel hand-hewn and river-smoothed, subtly uneven cupped hollows, cushioned rounded trench floors, the whole set reading as aged masonry and timeworn timber with a warm tactile roughness.

Chunky toy-like tabletop look: bold thick rounded rims, plump generously beveled tile corners, deep confident grooves and pillowy scooped reservoirs, playful oversized-feeling notches and lips, a friendly robust hand-filling heft that invites grabbing and stacking.

events.reason: Art direction calls for 'thick quarry-cut stone slabs with chiselled water channels,' 'hand-tooled canal masonry, never a flat printed board,' and a 'mason's yard' silhouette. Set B is the only one whose surfaces read as tooled/quarried stone relief (visible chisel-like tool-mark texture across board and tiles) rather than smooth machined plastic (set A) or plump toy-rounded plastic (set C); its board silhouette also most cleanly reads as a sunken stone basin with four spurs. Judged on form/surface-relief cues only, ignoring the color palette.
